clue.text: We're going through them, like a solver whose newsagent's run out of Telegraphs?

definitions.text: We're going through them, like a solver whose newsagent's run out of Telegraphs?

parts.words: We're going through them, like a solver whose newsagent's run out of Telegraphs
parts.note: hard periods we live through; read another way, a solver denied the Telegraph is giving a rival paper, The Times, a go

explanation.surface: A wry aside about difficult days, likened to the plight of a puzzler whose shop has sold out of their usual paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times is a rival British newspaper, so a Telegraph solver without their paper might be 'trying Times' instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A difficult period of hardship is commonly called a spell of trying times.

clue.text: Artistic group valued tips for De Nachtwacht painter holds up

parts.note: R.E.M. is an American rock band

indicators.note: the painter holds the reversed letters inside his name

parts.note: Georges Braque, French Cubist painter

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters read backwards

parts.note: to set a value on, as a price is set

indicators.note: the first letters of the two Dutch words

explanation.surface: An art collective's prize hints on the Dutch master behind The Night Watch are delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: De Nachtwacht (The Night Watch) is Rembrandt's own picture, a lure, but the painter here is Braque. 'up' reverses SET+DN to NDTES, which BRAQUE 'holds'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the manner of the Dutch master's art, so artistic in a particular style.

clue.text: Being horny, I start to bother old flame

indicators.note: the start of the word, its first letter

parts.note: an ex is a former lover

explanation.surface: An amorous confession: being aroused, someone thinks of pestering a former partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horny' suggests lust, but here it means having horns.
explanation.definitionFit: This mountain wild goat has large curving horns, so it is a horned creature.

clue.text: Has successful application for charity denied?

parts.note: one who applies and succeeds gains what was sought
aid is help given in charity

explanation.surface: Asks whether a charity grant has been approved or turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay a claim is to contradict or refuse it.

clue.text: Away from work, fish

definitions.meaning: read cryptically the word is a pair of fish: the ide (a carp, also spelt id in dictionaries) followed by the ling, a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone off work goes fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is cryptic: the answer splits as two fish, ID (a recognised variant spelling of IDE) and LING.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not working but lazing about is idling, as an engine idles without driving anything.

clue.text: A blast from the past to illustrate notice?

parts.note: e.g. introduces an example
an ad, advertisement, is a notice

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a vintage poster brought out as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blast' is an exclamation, not an explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic mild oath, an exclamation once common and now dated.

clue.text: Thus tallied totality entirely together?

parts.note: the last four words are each a way of saying 'everything', so one idea is given again and again, while every word starts with T

explanation.surface: A sum added up completely, all in one go.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 3,11 the answer reads ALL ITERATIVELY: tallied, totality, entirely and together are each a version of 'all'. 'Thus' points at the clue itself, whose words all begin with T.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's words share the opening letter T, so the clue is written in that repeated-initial style.

clue.text: Obsession in the Big Apple for lining border? Not at all

indicators.note: the pieces serve as a lining inside the word for border

parts.note: to abut is to border
nickname of New York, NY
having a thing about something is an obsession

explanation.surface: A New York fashion craze for lining borders, dismissed outright.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'New York thing' is a Big Apple obsession.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying it is anything but so is an emphatic way of denying it entirely.

clue.text: Flooring capacity at Ye Olde Crowne?

definitions.text: Flooring capacity at Ye Olde Crowne?

parts.words: Flooring capacity at Ye Olde Crowne
parts.note: an old-fashioned pub measure of drink, enough to knock a drinker to the floor; 'Ye Olde Crowne' suggests pre-metric, crown-era measures

explanation.surface: Seems to ask how much floor space a quaint old inn has.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flooring' looks like boards underfoot but means knocking someone out; the old British (imperial) measures predate metric, fitting a pub styled 'Ye Olde'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the British pre-metric unit of liquid volume, about 4.5 litres, a measure of capacity.

clue.text: Nibble tip of ear-lobe so much beau's titillated

indicators.note: excited, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: the 's reads as 'is', leaving beau as the fodder

indicators.note: the tip is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A flirt nibbles her sweetheart's ear and he is thoroughly aroused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nibble' looks romantic but is the definition. 'titillated' jumbles E plus SOMUCHBEAU.
explanation.definitionFit: A small appetiser served before a meal, literally 'mouth amuser', is a tasty morsel.

clue.text: Film family five days before assassination in Rome?

parts.note: Caesar was killed in Rome on the Ides of March, the 15th, so the month gives MAR
five days before the 15th is the 10th, X in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A film studio's family story dated just before Caesar's murder.
explanation.walkthrough: Together the pieces make a date, MAR X: March 10, five days before the Ides.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marx Brothers, Groucho, Harpo, Chico and siblings, were a celebrated comedy family of Hollywood movies.

clue.text: Argued coat of red should be removed altogether

indicators.note: the letters of red cover the rest like a coat, two at the front and one at the back
says the letters named next come out of the word for 'argued'

parts.note: to argue a case is to have reasoned it out

explanation.surface: Someone disputes whether a layer of red paint ought to be stripped off entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: RE comes off the front and D off the back of REASONED, the letters of 'red' wrapped round the rest like a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting together in unison, everyone doing something at once, is doing it as one.

clue.text: Time for Jack's girl finally to ditch him?

indicators.note: one letter stands in place of another, so the letter for time goes where one was
points to the last letter of the girl's name as the one exchanged

parts.note: Jack and Jill of the nursery rhyme

explanation.surface: Suggests it's time for Jack's girlfriend to end things with him at last.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads from Jill's side: to ditch her Jack.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon a sweetheart abruptly, ending the romance, is to throw them over.

clue.text: Ring concealed in party for English setter

indicators.note: the ring-shaped letter in the party word is covered over
one letter is exchanged for another

parts.note: a jolly is a party or outing
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: An English setter dog hidden among guests at a party with a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English setter' looks like the dog breed; 'setter' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This dessert sets firm as it cools, so in a crossword it can be called something that sets.

clue.text: Crapulent bishop with a proclivity for passing water?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

parts.words: with a proclivity for passing water
parts.note: oozy means apt to ooze, seeping moisture

explanation.surface: A hungover cleric with a weak bladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passing water' suggests urination but means seeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Crapulent means sick from excess drinking, and someone drunk is boozy.

clue.text: Hospital worker who's bound to welcome independent type

parts.note: SAN is short for sanatorium, a hospital

indicators.note: a word that welcomes another takes it inside

parts.note: a serf was a labourer bound to his lord's land

explanation.surface: A tied-in hospital employee who takes in a freelancer of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hospital worker' reads as one person, a porter or nurse, but splits in two. SAN, short for sanatorium, is crossword shorthand for a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A typeface without serifs is one kind of type, as used in printing.

clue.text: Keys ready for American golden oldie record label

definitions.meaning: the first notes of the sol-fa scale, so keys in a musical sense
'the ready' is cash, and do-re-mi is American slang for money

parts.note: d'or is an old expression meaning golden, as in Palme d'Or
EMI is a British record label

explanation.surface: A puzzling list: musical keys, American readiness and an old hit's record company.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions plus wordplay: D'OR ('of gold') is an old form for golden, and EMI is the record company.
explanation.definitionFit: The notes are the opening of the sol-fa scale, and in American slang the phrase means money, like 'dough'.

clue.text: This bhisti, a real guardian angel coming to grief

indicators.note: wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Describes a water carrier as a true protector who meets disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: A bhisti is an Indian water carrier. 'coming to grief' jumbles GUARDIAN ANGEL into the answer plus A REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's poem hero is a regimental water carrier in India, the very bhisti meant.

clue.text: Pluck odd selection of brollies to keep dry

indicators.note: the selected letters keep, that is hold, another piece inside
taking the odd-numbered letters of the following word

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol, i.e. dry

explanation.surface: Someone bravely sorts through umbrellas, picking a few to stay dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' looks like the umbrellas' job but means teetotal, TT.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, having courage or nerve is having bottle, the same as pluck.

clue.text: Crew on non-stop Munich train putting Zulu women in tight spot

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another comes after it
with no stop at the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Zug is German for train

indicators.note: the Zulu and women letters are put in among the others

parts.note: a gang is a crew
Z is Zulu in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A train crew in Bavaria lands some Zulu women in a fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-stop' cuts the end off the German word for train; 'putting ... in' places the Zulu and women letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess term borrowed from German for a position where any move worsens matters, hence a predicament.

clue.text: Will the Bees be playing with passion?

parts.note: an actor playing a role appears as that character
warm describes feeling with ardour

explanation.surface: Asks whether Brentford, nicknamed the Bees, will play their football with fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bees is the nickname of Brentford, a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees gathering in a crowd are swarming, the predicative adjective for teeming.

clue.text: Couples gripped by dolour: sadly, only one of the two bears up

definitions.text: only one of the two bears up

indicators.note: pairs of letters held within the two words that follow, two from each side of the colon

explanation.surface: Pairs in grief, and only one partner of the two copes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears up' looks like coping but means a bear in the sky above.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursa Major and Ursa Minor are the two Bear constellations; the shared Latin word names either one.

clue.text: Boerewors possibly having broken with its country tradition

indicators.note: parting company with something means losing it, so letters are dropped

parts.note: boerewors is a South African sausage, an example of one
SA, South Africa, home of boerewors

explanation.surface: A South African sausage strays from the recipe of its homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: Boerewors is a spiced farmer's sausage from South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Established custom or habitual practice is usage, i.e. tradition.

clue.text: Enigmatic clue? Not the first I put in place

indicators.note: the single-letter word is placed inside the rest
something enigmatic is puzzling, so the word beside it is jumbled
the opening letter of the clue word is dropped

explanation.surface: A solver mulls over a baffling clue they couldn't crack first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not the first' drops C from CLUE; 'Enigmatic' scrambles LUE to LEU, and 'put in' adds I.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In lieu of' means in place of, so the French-derived word is a synonym for stead.

clue.text: Letter R omitted centrally from 'mooring'

indicators.note: the letter is left out from the middle of the word

parts.note: a berth is a ship's mooring

explanation.surface: A note says the letter R was dropped from the middle of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Beth is the second character of the Hebrew alphabet, so it is one alphabetic letter.

clue.text: When cycling, fondly touch runners

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end to the other

parts.note: to kiss is to touch fondly

explanation.surface: A cyclist affectionately brushes past joggers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runners' are not athletes but the long blades worn in snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Skis are the narrow runners worn for gliding over snow.

clue.text: Domestic problem upsetting for hodman, I seek outside employment

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit outside, around another piece
upsetting the letters means jumbling them into a new order

parts.note: use and employment are synonyms

explanation.surface: A labourer's helper is upset when a colleague goes looking for another job.
explanation.walkthrough: A hodman carries bricks on a building site. 'upsetting for' jumbles HODMANISEEK, placed 'outside' USE.
explanation.definitionFit: This inflamed kneecap is named after household servants who knelt to scrub floors, a domestic's ailment.

clue.text: This nearly needed my quaintly personal view?

indicators.note: in a quaint, odd way, so the letters are rearranged
nearly all of the word, dropping its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone muses that they almost needed this oddly individual take on things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims NEEDED to NEEDE; 'quaintly' then jumbles THIS+NEEDE+MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagination pictures things only you can see, an inner, private vision.
